verses.text: This is the message of judgment against the wilderness by the sea. Like whirlwinds sweeping through the south, an enemy is coming from the wilderness, from a terrifying land.
I have been shown a terrible vision: the traitor betrays, and the destroyer destroys. Go up, Elam! Attack, Media! I will put an end to all the groaning Babylon caused.
So my body is filled with pain. Pains have grabbed me, like the pains of a woman giving birth. I am so troubled that I cannot hear. I am so terrified that I cannot see.
My heart is pounding, and fear makes me shake. The evening I longed for has become a time of trembling.
They set the table. They spread out the rugs. They eat and they drink. Get up, you commanders! Oil your shields!
For this is what the Lord said to me: "Go, post a watchman and have him report what he sees.
When he sees chariots with pairs of horsemen, riders on donkeys, or riders on camels, let him listen carefully, very carefully."
Then the watchman shouted like a lion: "Lord, I stand on the watchtower every day, and I stay at my post every night.
Look, here comes a chariot with a pair of horsemen!" Then he answered, "Fallen, fallen is Babylon! All the carved images of its gods lie broken on the ground!"
My people, crushed like grain on the threshing floor, I have told you what I heard from the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel.
This is the message of judgment against Dumah. Someone calls to me from Seir, "Watchman, how much of the night is left? Watchman, how much of the night is left?"
The watchman answers, "Morning is coming, but night is coming too. If you want to ask, then ask. Come back again."
This is the message of judgment against Arabia. You traveling groups of Dedanites, who camp in the thick bushes of Arabia,
bring water for the thirsty. You people of Tema, bring food for those running away.
For they are running from swords, from the drawn sword, from the bent bow, and from the heat of battle.
For this is what the Lord said to me: "Within one year, counted exactly as a hired worker counts the years, all the glory of Kedar will come to an end.
Only a few of the archers, the warriors of Kedar, will be left. The LORD, the God of Israel, has spoken."
